name: Mazapán
description: A crumbly, melt-in-the-mouth Mexican peanut candy pressed into rounds, iconic at every corner store.
ingredients: a handful of rehydrated dried chilies
a handful of fresh cilantro, chopped
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with lard.
In a large bowl, whisk together the masa dough and dried oregano until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the toasted pumpkin seeds with the orange juice until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 0 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
tips: Resist opening the oven door too early — a sudden change in temperature can cause the dessert to sink or crack.
This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
